selected.claim: Pinocchio implements publicly verifiable outsourced computation and measures prover and verifier costs across seven applications, demonstrating very small proofs and low verification time for the evaluated system.
selected.measurement_summary: 7 applications; 288-byte proof; ~10 ms verification; 19–60× prover-effort reduction versus prior work for the evaluated system
selected.boundary: Protocol-, implementation- and workload-specific; no universal cheap/fast-verification claim.

selected.claim: Practical Byzantine fault-tolerant state-machine replication can tolerate Byzantine faults under explicit replica and network assumptions, with optimizations evaluated experimentally.
selected.measurement_summary: BFT NFS implementation measured ~3% slower than standard unreplicated NFS on the Andrew benchmark in the reported environment; tolerates f Byzantine faults with 3f+1 replicas under stated assumptions
selected.boundary: Safety, liveness and performance depend on PBFT assumptions; not a universal recommendation for decentralized compute.

research_library.source_title: MapReduce: simplified data processing on large clusters
research_library.claim: A runtime can automatically partition data, schedule execution across many machines, handle machine failures and coordinate inter-machine communication for large data-processing workloads.
research_library.boundary: Distributed cluster execution under its workloads; not decentralized trust, multi-provider sovereignty or universal cost/performance superiority.

research_library.source_title: Chord: A scalable peer-to-peer lookup service for internet applications
research_library.claim: Chord provides decentralized key-to-node lookup with logarithmic communication and state scaling while adapting to joins and leaves.
research_library.boundary: Lookup protocol, not compute scheduler; does not establish workload throughput, execution correctness or economics.

research_library.source_title: Dynamo: Amazon's Highly Available Key-value Store
research_library.claim: Dynamo demonstrates a highly available distributed key-value design using partitioning, replication, object versioning and conflict resolution.
research_library.boundary: Storage architecture with availability trade-offs; not compute correctness or generic decentralized-compute SLO evidence.

research_library.source_title: Resilient Distributed Datasets: A Fault-Tolerant Abstraction for In-Memory Cluster Computing
research_library.claim: RDDs use immutable transformations and lineage to recover distributed in-memory datasets after failures.
research_library.boundary: Performance results are bounded to evaluated workloads and cluster implementation; not adversarial correctness or multi-provider decentralization.

research_library.claim: A distributed file system can provide fault tolerance and high aggregate performance when designed for explicit workload and hardware assumptions.
research_library.boundary: Google-specific workloads and environment; does not imply P2P decentralization or general performance claims.

research_library.source_title: Kademlia: A Peer-to-Peer Information System Based on the XOR Metric
research_library.claim: Kademlia uses an XOR metric and parallel asynchronous queries to locate nodes and data in a fault-prone peer-to-peer environment.
research_library.boundary: Peer discovery/routing only; not compute-task execution, result correctness, provider quality or marketplace performance.

research_library.source_title: In Search of an Understandable Consensus Algorithm
research_library.claim: Raft decomposes replicated-log consensus into leader election, log replication and safety with overlapping-majority membership change.
research_library.boundary: Crash-fault consensus, not Byzantine fault tolerance or compute verification.

research_library.source_title: BOINC: A System for Public-Resource Computing and Storage
research_library.claim: BOINC provides an architecture for public-resource computing across heterogeneous volunteer resources and applications.
research_library.boundary: Does not prove trustless result correctness, deterministic performance, guaranteed availability or marketplace economics.

research_library.claim: Intel SGX defines a hardware-assisted enclave model intended to protect integrity and confidentiality of security-sensitive computation.
research_library.boundary: Attestation binds platform/enclave properties; does not prove application-level correctness or freedom from side channels.

context_library.boundary: Implementation-contribution capability only; not production security efficacy, vulnerability reduction or decentralized-compute performance.
